name: Insulator Creek Falls
description:
14/08/22: Insulator Creek Falls
A one-day bushwalk on Bambaroo Track to Insulator Creek canyon. Amazing giant trees and great rainforest scenes.  
Leader: Cherry Judge
Image credit @wanderstories
Rated: Medium. Steep bush tracks, uneven footings, with some off-track creek walking and wet rocks. About 8 hours bushwalking. 

Meeting: Walk leader to let you know when you RSVP

Walk Description: The Bambaroo Track starts near the highway and climbs steeply up the range spurs to the top of the Paluma range. But today we will only go halfway up. The first hour is a hot steep road climb to get the heart pumping and sweat flowing. Then we enter the rainforest and the climb continues along a rainforest track, but less steep, to reach the start of the giant fig trees. These trees are amazing. 
 
After exploring one of the giant trees (there are at least 9 giant figs in the area, but will only visit a few), we continue to more fascinating trees of a different types. Then more track climbing up the range, to reach the Insulator Creek track. Steep rough track descending to the creek to amazing scenes. The terrain includes uneven footings, rock hopping, bush bashing, steep climbs, and some exposed ledges. 
 
The return journey is the same route but downhill most of the way. 
 
Full day walk. Estimate back at the carpark around 4 to 5 pm.
     
What to bring: 
Day pack, food/snacks for the day, water 2 to 3 lt minimum (refill from the creek at midday or carry 4 lt water for all day), long sleeve clothing and good rugged footwear (to protect from sun, scratches, stings, and bites), electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic), and sunglasses. Also, head torch and whistle. 
 
If you are uncomfortable using creek water for drinking water refill (after treating suitably), then carry 4 lt min for the day, or more to suit your requirements. Note that the club recommends that any natural water sources must be suitably treated before consumption. 
 
Fees: non-members $5 
 
Must be over 18yrs to participate.    

To RSVP, email the club at info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

name: Paradise Beach & Castle Rock
description:
The next Club walk will be held on 15 May to Paradise Beach & Castle Rock. 
Wilfred Karnoll is the leader  

The walk commences at the end of Cape Cleveland Road and follows a rough, but well-defined track around the perimeter of AIMS and hits the northern end of the AIMS beach.  From there it's up and over the saddle, and through the coastal forest to the Little Beach.  Again, this is a marked track and ascends about 60 m at the most.  Enjoy the views once you get to the saddle of Little Beach and beyond.  

The shoreline has changed so much at Little Beach since we first went there in the early 2010s after the big monsoonal rains about 4 years ago.  It's still a beautiful little spot though.  About half way along the beach a second creek flows down to it and you'll make your way up the creek then cross over to the northern bank and follow the track all the way to the second saddle.  There is a great lookout to your right , but it's a little bit off the beaten track.  The descent to Paradise Beach is straight forward and follows a track.  

Castle Rock is at the northern end of the beach, you will either enjoy a long stroll along the beach followed by a very steep ascent to the Rock or cut inland in order to take a more gradual ascent to Castle Rock.  Don't worry you'll still get the steep scramble at the end no matter which way you go!  Your heart rate will be ever so elevated by the time you hit the high point and see spectacular views to the north and south of you.  Enjoy your lunch at the summit and prepare yourself for the journey back to the cars.  The return journey largely follows the same route, but there are often a couple of alternative routes to use to leave Castle Rock.  Whatever you do, don't be tempted if the word "Balancing" is used.  That's another story though.  

What do you bring?  Well, it's the usual requirements for a day walk.  Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent.  Long sleeved shirts, long trousers or shorts with gaiters will protect you from the sun and scratches.  Morning tea, lunch and afternoon tea, plus sundry snacks to sustain you throughout the day.  First aid kit and a snake bandage are always essentials.  Camera.  Togs & towel to have a swim at Paradise Beach.  

Water.  I would suggest 3 - 4 L as it will be a long walk and although there has been recent rain we have never assumed the water supply is reliable.

Please call Wilfred to nominate for the walk or email Contact info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.    Wilfred reserves the right to refuse permission to join the walk if he thinks it would be unsuitable for you.  We would rate this walk as an easy to medium, yet long day walk.

name: Echo Creek and K Traverse
description:
Next Walk Sunday May 30 

Echo Creek & K Track, Paluma.   

Leader Luen Warneke.  To register or for more info 0415 947 748 or luenwarneke@gmail.com 

Meeting Place: Paluma Village Green @ 8 am.  

This Sunday we will go faraway in time to Echo Beach rather I mean Creek.   Luen will lead us on yet another creek based adventure.  If it is anything like the Cloudy/Ethel adventure we will experience beautiful forest country; very attractive creek scenery; be in the creek as part of the scenery enjoying the anti-inflammatory properties of the creek (i.e. over knee deep in water).  There will no doubt be parts where there will be out of creek off track walking and need to divide a way for ourselves via wait-a-while.   


The plan is very loose: we’ll meet in Paluma and drove to the Dam road and park at the start of the K-Track, walk to the headwaters of Echo Creek and follow the creek downstream.  As indicated earlier you will most likely get your feet wet, so choose your footwear wisely.  You don’t want to wear anything that will slip when wet.  We will be in and out of the creek, finding the best route possible.  As always there will be rainforest plants involved so be prepared to divide a way through it (seceteurs).  We’ll stop for morning tea, lunch and hopefully afternoon tea.   Once we’ve had enough of the creek we’ll rejoin the K-track and follow it back to the cars.  We’ll be back at the cars between 3 and 5 pm.    

Bring your hat, sunscreen, insect repellent & shoes that you don’t mind getting wet.  Long sleeved shirts are recommended to protect yourself from scratches and the sun.  Some people wear long pants, others shorts with gaiters: the choice is yours.   

First aid kit, snake bandage, water 2 – 3 L.  Refill from the creek, but it is also an idea to bring water purification tablets.  If you’re not happy with drinking creek water – treated or not - bring 4 L for the day.  Morning tea, lunch, afternoon tea.  Other snacks.  Gifts and other tributes for walk leader and any of the committee members who happen to be on the walk.  Camera, togs & towel.  Change of clothes for the journey home is a good idea.  Even if not car pooling you could be soaked and getting into clean dry clothes is really nice at the end of a walk.   

It is wise to bring a dry bag to put store the gear you’ll take on the walk that you do not want to get wet.   

Visitors must pay a $5 visitor fee and sign an acknowledgement of risk form.  You must be over 18 to participate.   

For gleam more information and details on the walk & to register for it please contact Luen directly.

name: Cloudy Creek and Ethel Creek
description:
Sunday 16th May – Another Luen-Led Adventure
Cloudy and Ethel Creek Explore (Paluma area). Off-track rainforest creek exploration. 
Leader – Luen. To register or for more info contact the walk leader
Type of walk – half to full day exploration bushwalking. Walk will be around ~10+ km. Track at start and end of day – but will be several hours off-track exploring the creeks and walking through rainforest, viewing lovely creek scenery. Route map: https://maps.wanderstories.space/?id=1620711096583#-19.00408,146.1967,15z,outdoor,alertsQld/articles
In Brief: Walk on Collins' Track to where it meets and crosses Cloudy Creek, then go down stream to Cloudy Creek Falls (off track). Walk on-track to Ethel Creek Falls. Walk up stream along Ethel Creek and then off-track to the Paluma Ewen Road. Walk back along the road to the village. 

This wonderful walk will start and end in Paluma village.  The tracks that will be used at various stages of this walk (Collins’ and the Paluma-Ethel Falls Tracks) pass through very scenic rainforest terrain; the off-track portion, particularly down Crystal Creek is straight through the rainforest, where Luen will be busy looking for the best route.  This is what off-track is all about.  Be aware it could be a little bit overgrown in places and there may be some thorns, etc., from various vines and other shrubs, hence the need for some protective clothing.  It may be necessary at times to walk in the creek itself, so wet feet are a definite possibility.  Ethel Creek Falls is quite spectacular and makes a great backdrop for a photograph; Did we mention its also a great swimming spot?  Well it is, just what tired bodies need.  After this we’ll be going through the forest (off-track) to get back to the main road.  You will WALK back to Paluma village because no self-respecting driver would stop for a rag tag bunch like us: so no thumbs out to try and hitch a lift back you slackers.  

Cost – non-members $5 fee. 
 
What you need – carry water (minimum 2 lt), refill from creek as required (treat / filter your water refill).  Due to our proximity to Paluma Village we never can be 100% sure about the water, so we do recommend that if you are comfortable drinking straight from the creek you bring something to treat the water.  Tablets like iodine or chlorine, or even a filter should work fine.  The alternative is to bring about 4 L for the whole day.  

Lunch,  snacks / energy food, electrolytes, hat, sunscreen, insect repellent (to keep the leeches & mozzies at bay), enclosed sturdy footwear, personal first kit. Recommend long sleeve clothing / gaiters to avoid scratches. Some members also wear fingerless gloves. Hiking poles are good on track walks and sometimes when crossing creeks; on off-track sections they are probably best secured in your pack.  
 
Note – footwear will get wet, so wear foot wear that is suitable.  
 
Timing and meet – Meet Paluma Village Green at the car park near the toilet block at 8 am. 
Estimated Completion – back at the car park around 2-5 pm depending on group size, how  long we spend off track (due to vegetation/terrain), amount of breaks, and fitness levels.
 
Must be over 18yrs to participate.  It’s not that we don’t like youngsters, but visitors are considered temporary members and to be a member you have to be over 18.  

In addition Luen must approve your registration for the walk – if he thinks based on the information you provide him or based on the types of walks you’ve done that this isn’t the best option for you, he has the right veto your nomination.  This is a safety precaution the Club takes.

name: High Camp / Terraces / St Margaret’s Creek
description:
Pre-Registration / approval with the walk leader is essential. Walks have been popular, so register ASAP to reserve a spot. 

To register or more info, contact the walk leader - Luen 0415 947 748 or email luenwarneke@gmail.com. 
Keith will also be a secondary walk leader.

Meet point – Bruce Hwy, opposite Alligator Creek roadhouse at 0730 (cnr Bentley Drive and Bruce Hwy). Then we will drive to the bushwalk start point. Walk starts from private property (no public access).

Fees: non-members $5 

Walk Description: 
The standard Terraces walk, start on track, then major part is off track bushwalking and rockhopping. Some cliff / ledges, and steep hills, loose surfaces, to climb / scramble.  More information at https://wanderstories.space/the-terraces/

The challenge this time of year is seepage and slippery rocks. Usually we don’t go this time of year as conditions are not ideal (we have done it in the past this time of year with varying degrees of success or not). However, if we can get into the middle of the Terraces, the waterfalls are even more spectacular this time of year. 

If conditions are not suitable we have options, which may include the Rockslides area, and explore down St Margarets Creek to Black Rock area and further downstream. This creek area is scenic, nice pools and cascades, and worth exploring. We will see what weather and conditions are like on the day. 

Full day walk. Estimate back at the cars around 4 to 5 pm.

What to bring - Food / snacks for the day, water 2 lt minimum (refill from creeks or carry 4 lt water), electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic). Some members also wear fingerless gloves. Hiking poles are good on track walks but not so good in bushbashing - but are good if in the creek and for creek crossings - balance assist. If you are uncomfortable using creek water for drinking water refill (after treating suitably), then carry 4 lt min for the day, or more to suit your requirements. Note that the club recommends that any natural water sources must be suitably treated before consumption. 

Clothing- as it off-track bushwalking and exploring, long sleeve clothing or gaiters is recommended. Otherwise you may have cuts/scratches on exposed skin at the end of the day. 

Footwear  - sturdy shoes that provide decent grip on slippery rocks are suitable.

Must be over 18yrs old to participate.

name: Blue Gum Circuit (Paluma)
description:
SUNDAY 7 February 2021

Blue Gum Circuit: A great track walk on the Blue Gum Creek circuit. The club developed this track back in 2013. You'll see waterfall and creek scenery, rainforest and woodland, old tin mining areas and enjoy a lovely swim or two. There is a steep 400 mr elevation climb back to Paluma village though.

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: hard (due to the elevation gain).

DESCRIPTION
This track walk starts in Paluma village before descending on the south side of Paluma into the Blue Gum / upper Star Valley area. There will be several steep descents. At the bottom, we'll walk and rockhop alongside creeks. There will be a couple of creeks that require crossing (one with boots off) and others that require rock hopping skills. Our efforts will be rewarded with a swim at the lagoon at lunch time - one of the great lagoons we visit.  
 
After lunch – the climb back to Paluma is a 3 hour 400m elevation climb up a steep bush track. We'll stop at Triple Falls on the way for another swim or to just enjoy the scenery.

FITNESS

name: Double Barrel Creek
description:
SUNDAY 31 January
 
REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.
 
RATED - Hard
Although this should be a relatively flat walk (except for track walk home from Crystal Creek Falls) expect off track walking, slippery rocks, creek crossings/creek walking, thick rainforest etc.
 
DESCRIPTION
A major part of this adventure is off-track rainforest and creek walking down Double Barrel Creek to Blue Lagoon then Crystal Creek Falls. 
This is an explorative walk. We'll start on track from the dam (1hr). From there we'll head to the headwaters of Double Barrel Creek, then walk down the creek - either along side in rainforest, or in the creek itself (probably both). On reaching Crystal Creek junction, it'll be a short walk downstream to Blue Lagoon for a swim. After that, it's a short stroll through rainforest and cascades to Crystal Creek Falls. Heading home will be back on track for the 1.5 hr walk uphill back to the dam. Along the way there may be tangled vines to negotiate - love the rainforest!

description:

name: Paluma Range Traverse (3 days)
description:
The Paluma Range traverse is a fantastic 3 day, 35 km track walk with mountain creeks, lookouts, waterfalls, world heritage wet tropics rainforest, and camping at nice creeks.

WHEN
October Long Weekend 3rd-5 th Saturday to Monday

WALK DESCRIPTION
A fantastic 3 day, 35 km hike to traverse the Paluma Range rainforest tracks system, from Paradise Lagoon (Mutarnee) to Jourama Falls. The route follows rainforest mountain tracks.

Day 1 is a 10 km hike, cross Crystal Creek, pass nice mountain creeks, climb up Bullocky Toms track, via Cloudy Lookout and Gold Ck Falls (top spot!) to camp at Johnstone’s Clearing, a wonderful rainforest camp spot next to a rainforest creek. It is approx an 800 mr ascent. So yes, it is a steep climb up Bullocky Toms Track (2 to 3 hrs continual steep up from Cairn Ck to Gold Ck Falls).

Day 2 is a nice undulating 15 km rainforest walk through the top of the range. But the undulations means still an overall ascent over the day of 450 mr with overall descent is 540 mr – call it flattish then ! Pass through DCK Hut, Mt Spec, Prospector Creek, to camp at Station Creek, adjacent to a rainforest creek.

Day 3 is a wonderful day,  only 11 km, all downhill after the first hour or so, to Waterview Ck. Maybe detour to Black Hole Falls. Then reach the amazing top of Jourama Falls. The finale is to descend the slopes with great views of Jourama Falls as you descend, to reach the car park. Total descent of 1,000 mr (ascent of 300 over the day), there are some steep down bits. Oh, after the top of Jourama Falls, there is a short steep climb though before the finale descent  J

Whilst a track walk, it can be on rough rainforest tracks with tree roots, uneven footing, and rocks at times.

WHAT YOU NEED TO BRING
You need to be self sufficient for 3 days of walking and camping.
- Hiking / Camping gear – keep it light (recommend lightweight shelter (tent/tarp) with insect protection, lightweight mattress and sleeping bag/quilt, cooking gear)
-  Insect repellent
- Sun protections: hat, sunscreen, long sleeve clothing
- Hiking poles will be handy for some walkers.
- Water  – generally only need to carry 2 lt of water during the day, but have capacity for 4 lt. Refill from rainforest creeks (recommend treat / filter water refills). Electrolytes are recommended.
- Camp clothes recommended - include a fleece or something warm for nights (some also take thermals as nights can be chilly). Wet weather gear.
- Food and drinks for 3 days
- Personal first aid kit

Any questions about hiking / camping gear suitability, feel free to ask Wilfred (walk leader)

WHEN

Finish: Monday 5/10 - Back at cars approx 5pm

description:

WALK SUMMARY:  this is one of our easier walks suitable for those new to bushwalking, or just wanting an easier day. You still need reasonable bushwalking fitness especially for the walk back to the Dam carpark which is the hardest part. It is still a great bushwalk with good highlights.  

This walk will be a rainforest track walk from Paluma dam to Crystal Creek falls (top) via Rock Garden.  Whilst a track walk, it is a rough rainforest track with tree roots, uneven footing, and rocks at times, and a few steep bits. Calling all paddlers. Join us for a leisurely cruise up the Ross River. The plan is to launch from Loam Island and paddle upstream for 1-1.5hrs before returning. BYO vessel and gear.

WHEN: Saturday 1 August, ready for a 7:15am departure. We plan to back by 10:30am.

WHERE: Loam Island (BOAT RAMP). There is ample parking here but please park out of the way of cars with boat trailers.

WHAT TO BRING:
A ‘seaworthy’ kayak/canoe + related gear (eg paddle, gloves, PFD if required)
Water + food
Sun protective clothing and hat
Sunscreen, insect repellent
Waterproofing for anything that needs to stay dry
Shoes suitable to get wet for entry/exit 
Container to collect rubbish (optional)

FACILITIES: There is a toilet located close by, picnic tables

COST:
Visitors/non members = $5 

WHO:
Anyone who would like to come. Beginners welcome if you have access to a kayak/canoe. This is planned to be a social paced paddle to explore some of the river. If you would like a fast paddle please consider if this event is right of you. We will keep together in a rough group.

name: Mt Storth (pls read event description)
description:
SUNDAY 19th July - Mt Storth (full day)

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED - Hard
Approx. 9hrs bushwalking. There is a long steep hill climb, no track, long grass, uneven footings, scrub, with return home via a creek rock hop.

DESCRIPTION
Mt Storth is the northern summit of the Mt Elliot range of Bowling Green Bay National Park (north of Alligator Ck). It is 632m altitude. To summit, it is a steep climb up a long spur without a track.  Whilst scrubby at the lower reaches, the vegetation changes as we climb towards the summit. Lunch will be at the summit and depending on what time we get there, there are two ways we could descend. The most likely is via Killymoon Creek (a good rock hop, boulder scramble and nice cascades) or if time is short we'll go down Dribble Creek (rock hop, boulder scramble also but shorter).

The walk commences and traverses private property and then enters the national park.

FITNESS
To be suitable for this walk, a good analogy would be doing a Castle Hill spur, without a track, three times with ease before lunchtime.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for full day eg minimum 4L
- Clothing: there is a lot of long grass and scrub so full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Swimming gear (if we come down Killymoon there may be opportunity for a swim at the main pool)

Must be over 18years to participate

To discuss suitability, to register or for more information please contact tsvbush@hotmail.com and we will get back to you asap.

name: FULL - Dalrymple Gap Walking Track (pls read event description)
description:
Registrations for this walk have closed as walk capacity has been reached. 

SATURDAY 18th July  – Dalrymple Gap track 16 km. Full day.

RATED – EASY . National Park track walk with creek crossings and a hill.
REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL.
PLEASE READ ALL OF THE INFORMATION BELOW.

It's a great time of year to walk the Dalrymple Gap track. The creek is still flowing and temperatures are not too hot. This walk will be an out and back walk from the southern access point to the old bridge return.

A detailed walk description and history is on the QLD Govt Parks and Forests website. https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/dalrymple-gap/about
This historic route is a nice 8km rainforest  track walk from southern end following the creek, then up a hill to the historic old stone bridge at top of range. There are several creek crossings and if there is water above rocks will have to wade (last Saturday the rocks were under water at first crossing). At the bridge, we turn around and return by same route. There is an opportunity for a swim at a pool.

To comfortably enjoy this walk you should be able to complete Castle Hill and be confident with the distance.

WHEN – Sunday 18th July

0830 Meet at walk start Southern Access point (Ingham  end, near Broadwater). The last five kilometres of road is unsealed, but can be accessed using a conventional vehicle. Driving directions at this link (allow 2 hrs drive) :

https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/dalrymple-gap/visiting-safely

If you wish to follow Keith (walk leader) from Ingham, meet at McDonalds Ingham at 0745.

We should be back at the cars by 1600. Then 2 hr drive home.

WHAT TO BRING:

Bring snacks / food for morning tea and lunch.

Water – carry drinking water for 1 day walking – at a minimum 2 lt water and refill from creek as required (treat the water). 

Clothing – recommend long sleeve clothing. Small day pack. Hat, sunscreen, insect repellent. 

Footwear – enclosed footwear suitable for rock hopping / bushwalking. Swimming costume or similar for the pool swim.

First Aid kit - we recommend you carry a small personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister treatment supplies.

COST:
Non-members $5 walk fee.

Must be 18yrs or over to participate.

Please read all of the information below. Registration is essential - see below for details. Thanks.

KILLYMOON CREEK is an ideal half-day walk for an introduction to creek based bushwalking.

It's a great time of year to try Killymoon as it will be flowing but easily walkable. It's a pretty creek with small cascades along the creek and a good pool at the turn around point.

WHAT THE WALK INVOLVES: 
We'll be walking up a creek with rockhopping, boulder scrambling, and traversing rock ledges alongside cascades. The walk to the creek is part track, with a hill to cross.

MEETING TIME + DUARTION:
Meet time 0800 at Alligator Creek (exact location will be given when you register for the walk as it's a private residence).
We should be back at the cars around 1300, but don’t plan anything until much later.

WHAT TO BRING:
Bring snacks / food for morning tea at the creek pool. If you're someone who gets hungry perhaps bring an extra snack incase we're late returning.

Water – carry drinking water for ½ day walking – at a minimum 2 lt water and refill from creek as required (treat the water).

Clothing – recommend long sleeve clothing. Small day pack. Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent.

Footwear – enclosed footwear suitable for rock hopping / bushwalking. Swimming costume or similar for the pool swim.

A basic first aid kit including a snake bandage and blister kit are recommended.

description:
Our plan is to walk out to Cape Cleveland (groups departing both Friday 2/8 and Saturday 3/8) for the weekend, returning Sunday 4/8.
The beauty of this walk is that we can access part of the route through AIMS (no access to the general public) and carry only our day packs.  Enroute we'll have great views over the Cape, Townsville and Maggie Is. If we're lucky we may even spot a whale!  
The walk will be partly on rough bush track and offtrack with terrain that is often hilly and rocky with long grass. 
Participants are required to provide all their equipment though and be self sufficient.  Camping gear and food will be transported to the Cape by boat (see below for cost).

For a detailed briefing or to RSVP contact Wilfred or Phil (details distributed via email 15/7) or email tsvbush@hotmail.com.

description:
This walk starts from the Jourama Falls carpark and passes the upper falls lookout.  There is a very steep climb to the top of the escarpment, then a brief bush-bash down a gully into the walkable part of the creek upstream of the main falls.  There is a long (and not entirely straightforward) rock-hop / scramble up the creek to a five-star swimming hole with a small waterfall which we will reach in time for lunch.   We are also going to go to the Black Hole (finally).  We will be returning via the track that has been cut to the Black Hole.  

This will be a full day walk
For more info or to RSVP please contact Keith or contact tsvbush@hotmail.com (by Friday).

name: The Terraces
description:
This walk will see us clambering beside about 10 – 15 waterfalls, depending on how far we get. We start from Private Property and make our way onto a powerline easement over very level country then we hit the national park. We travel along Palm Creek and then descend into the creek at the Princess Pool. Our journey then goes up one of the tributaries of Palm Creek (we can see it from the highway on our drive there). We do have to climb around several waterfalls (clambering up beside them). There is some exposure on some ascents but there are sufficient hand and foot holds to get us up and down safely.

We normally return the way we came, but taking a detour up to the rock slides for afternoon tea. Then it is back the way we came to our starting point. This walk does have its challenges, but it is not a particularly difficult walk. The clambering is not technical climbing, but you do have to gain some height in this manner.

For more information or to RSVP by Saturday 20/7: contact Phil (details distributed via email 15/7) or email the club at tsvbush@hotmail.com.
